attempts_list.attack: Round-3 finding 16 replay (custom masker that RETURNS an error quoting the value it could not mask), plus the two neighbouring module-boundary cases my brief names: a masker that panics halfway with the value in the panic string, a masker that panics with an *error* quoting the value, and a masker that returns its input unchanged. Registered against the public mask module in a separate Go module.
attempts_list.reproduction:

# main.go registers, all under mask.CatEmail, with canary "victim.canary@bigcorp.example":
#   erroring:    return mask.Value{}, fmt.Errorf("cannot mask %q: unsupported shape", in.Text)
#   panicking:   panic(fmt.Sprintf("halfway through %s", in.Text))
#   panicErr:    panic(fmt.Errorf("halfway: %s", in.Text))
#   passthrough: return in, nil

go run .
attempts_list.fix:
FIXED, no fix owed. Output, all four value-free:
  rt4_error     err=the masker returned an error: category email: masker rt4_error returned an error of type *errors.errorString (its message is withheld because it may quote the value)
  rt4_panic     err=the masker panicked: category email: masker rt4_panic panicked with a value of type string (it is withheld because it may quote the value)
  rt4_panicerr  err=the masker panicked: category email: masker rt4_panicerr panicked with an error of type *errors.errorString (...)
  rt4_pass      err=the masker's output follows the value it was given, so the cell was not masked: category email: masker rt4_pass
In every case res.Out.Text is "" and res.Masked is false. T-0223 (commit 4ca95ff) added mask.ErrMaskerFailed and the maskCell wrapper the round-3 report asked for, so the module keeps its own contract without relying on the parent binary's redaction (ADR-006). One cosmetic gap, not a leak: internal/transform/codes.go maskReason's sentinel list has no mask.ErrMaskerFailed entry, so at the CLI this refusal renders as the generic `an error of type *fmt.wrapError` rather than the sentinel's own words — value-free either way, but less diagnostic than the other six.

attempts_list.attack: NEW VARIANT of finding 16, against the T-0223 fix itself: a custom masker that returns an error which quotes the value AND wraps one of the mask module's own sentinels — `fmt.Errorf("cannot fit %q: %w", in.Text, mask.ErrNoRoom)`. maskCell's new wrapper is gated on isModuleError(err), which is an errors.Is/As test the masker controls, so declaring the module's sentinel buys the masker a pass straight through the redaction.
attempts_list.fix:
LEAKED at the module boundary. mask.Apply returns the third-party masker's message, canary and all, out of the public module — the exact egress T-0223 closed, reopened through the escape hatch the fix added. Root cause: mask/mask.go maskCell does `if isModuleError(err) { return Value{}, err }` before wrapping, and isModuleError (mask/mask.go:283) is errors.Is over the module's seven sentinels plus errors.As over NoRoomError/DomainError — every one of which a hostile or careless masker can wrap around its own free-form text. The exemption exists for a real reason (T-0223's round-4 replay R3-1: wrapping unconditionally broke errors.Is(err, ErrNoRoom) for internal/transform's exit-code text), but it was implemented as 'pass the whole error object through' when only the *identity* needed to survive.

Not a live CLI leak today, for the same reason round 3 recorded finding 16 as a contract break rather than an incident: no masker is loadable at runtime (THREAT_MODEL.md T4/T7), and internal/transform/codes.go reasonSummary/maskReason deliberately print *the sentinel's own text* rather than the wrapper's — maskReason's comment even names this exact attack ('a masker is free to wrap mask.ErrNoRoom with the row in its message, and errors.Is would say yes to that too'). So the tree knows about the hole one layer up and defends there, while the module that owns the contract does not. THREAT_MODEL.md names no such residual; T4's §193 paragraph claims the module keeps its own contract for programs that import it directly (ADR-006), which is the promise this breaks, so documented_residual is false.

Fix: never return a foreign error object. In maskCell, always construct the module's own error and carry only the identity across — e.g. `return Value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: category %s: masker %s returned %s", sentinelOf(err), cat, id, panicKind(err))` where sentinelOf(err) returns the matched module sentinel (or ErrMaskerFailed when none matched), so errors.Is(err, ErrNoRoom) still answers yes and errors.As still reaches a *module-built* NoRoomError/DomainError reconstructed from the masker's typed fields (Category, ID, TypeTag, MaxLen — all value-free by construction), while the masker's own string is dropped on the floor. Add a mask/apply_guards_test.go case that registers a masker wrapping each of the seven sentinels with a canary in its message and asserts the canary is absent from err.Error() while errors.Is still holds; that is the assertion the current tests are missing, and it is what would have caught this.

THREAT_MODEL.md's A2b bullet says unknownColumnsBesideCertain 'masks such a column as free_text in any table holding a column at certain under a category that identifies a person'; the email column is certain, the rail fires on the `text` control and masks correctly, and the only difference in the leaking run is the declared length. internal/classify/classify.go:1527 `const minUnknownLen = 16` with the comment 'char(4), varchar(8) and the rest are status codes, currency codes and short keys, and free_text's filler does not fit in them' — but a short declared length is not evidence a column is impersonal: a given name, a surname, a postcode, a national ID and a phone number all fit in varchar(12), and an attacker (or an ordinary schema author) picks the length. attempts_list.fix: Documented residual, THREAT_MODEL.md T2, the bullet "**The residual, stated rather than closed.**": "Neither control stops an application from writing to the target: an advisory lock coordinates only clients that ask for it ... What is closed is narrower and is the thing the review found: no lazyslice run destroys a table on a verdict that has stopped being true, and no two lazyslice runs take one target apart together." Nothing was destroyed and no second run took part, so what is claimed closed stayed closed. Two things that sentence's own reasoning does not cover and that are worth correcting: (a) it explains the residual as a writer "blocked by the lock until then" and afterwards writing "into the fresh table lazyslice created" -- that is only true of tables in the plan; a table created outside the plan is never locked and never rechecked, so the writer is not blocked at all and the rows are not lazyslice's own. (b) The run still exits 0 and writes `complete` over a database that its own gate would refuse as not empty, so the operator is handed a target that is part fake and part production with a green exit. Cheap fix, inside the lease that is already held: before the first drop, re-run the gate's own emptiness probe over the target's *current* user-table set (not the plan's), under the run lease, and refuse `load.refused.target_changed` naming the tables that appeared. That is one extra `SELECT EXISTS` sweep on a target the gate has already sized (<=2,000 tables) and it makes the recheck a statement about the database the gate approved rather than about the subset this run intends to touch. If that is judged too costly, the T2 residual bullet should at least be amended to say that a table created outside the plan is outside the lock-and-recheck entirely, and the run should degrade to a non-zero exit or a printed warning instead of a silent exit 0.

attempts_list.fix:
Not named anywhere in THREAT_MODEL.md or ARCHITECTURE.md: neither file mentions a replica or a standby as a source (the only standby mention is T9's `max_standby_streaming_delay` cancellation), and T2's identity rule is written entirely in terms of one postmaster reached under several spellings. Three changes.
(1) internal/pg's cluster identity treats the postmaster start time as decisive on disagreement. That is wrong for exactly this shape: a differing start time proves the two POSTMASTERS differ, which is not the same as proving the two CLUSTERS differ -- a hot standby is a different postmaster of the same cluster, and in a primary/standby pair the start times ALWAYS differ. When `system_identifier` is missing on one side, a start-time disagreement should downgrade the verdict to unknown (which sameClusterVerdict already answers as `true`, possibly the source's own cluster) rather than to a confident "different". That is the same fail-closed reasoning ARCHITECTURE.md line 1053 already applied in the opposite direction for the oid and the version: only some fields are specific enough to prove sameness, and here the start time is not specific enough to prove difference.
(2) Add a positive replica check, which is cheap, needs no privilege and is decisive: read `pg_is_in_recovery()` on the source (executable by PUBLIC) and, when it is true, read `sender_host`/`sender_port` from `pg_stat_wal_receiver` where readable, or at minimum print a header line saying the source is a standby. A run whose source is a standby and whose target is not the same server should say so; today lazyslice cannot tell an operator that the database it just wrote to is the primary feeding the database it just read.
(3) Land round-2 fix item 3, still not landed: ARCHITECTURE.md's recommended-role snippet (lines 1093-1097) still contains only CONNECT/USAGE/SELECT, with line 1041 claiming "the identity works without it". The variant below measures that claim and finds it false for this shape. Add `GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION pg_control_system() TO lazyslice_ro;` to the snippet and to internal/core/run.go's CodeRoleWritable message.
Regression test: internal/pg/gate_integration_test.go should assert that a source on a standby and a target on that standby's primary yield SameCluster == true under a role that cannot execute pg_control_system().

attempts_list.fix: With the grant, `system_identifier` is filled on both sides and decides alone, so the standby and its primary are correctly recognised as one cluster and the warning fires. The write still proceeds, which is the documented design for an explicitly named --target (ADR-013). This is the direct evidence that ARCHITECTURE.md line 1041's claim -- "`EXECUTE` on `pg_control_system` is still not granted to `PUBLIC` and this rule does not ask for it: the identity works without it" -- is false for a primary/standby pair, and that the recommended-role snippet at lines 1093-1097 must carry the GRANT.

attempts_list.attack: NEW, wrong-target surface item "a target URL taken from a compose file that points at prod", combined with the replica finding to reach the unsupervised path ADR-013 exists to close: a headless run (`--yes`) with NO --target, in a project directory whose compose file and environment name a production DSN. --source is the standby; the ladder's rung-2 environment candidate ($DATABASE_URL) is a database on the production primary. ADR-013's second escalation in internal/core's openTarget refuses a ladder-chosen target only when the GATE says same cluster -- the verdict the replica attack defeats -- so the escalation never fires.
attempts_list.reproduction:
mkdir -p $B/proj && cd $B/proj
cat > docker-compose.yml <<'EOF'
name: shopapp
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:16
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:15600/newprod
EOF
psql postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:15600/app -c "REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION pg_control_system() FROM reader;"   # back to stock privileges
psql postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:15600/postgres -c 'DROP DATABASE newprod' -c 'CREATE DATABASE newprod'
psql postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:15600/newprod -f $B/schema.sql
export LAZYSLICE_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
export DATABASE_URL='postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:15600/newprod'
$B/lazyslice --source 'postgres://reader:pw@127.0.0.1:15601/app' --yes --no-config -n 5      # no --target

OBSERVED (exit 0):
  docker: no compose project for this directory - showing all Postgres containers
  $DATABASE_URL: postgres@127.0.0.1:15600/newprod - postgres 14, 2 table(s), probably empty
  container lsdev16: ... not empty
  ... dropping public.orders in the target / dropping public.customers in the target
  public.customers: 5 rows / public.orders: 20 rows
grep -c 'same cluster' = 0
psql -tA postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:15600/newprod -c 'select count(*) from customers'  -> 5
  -> headless, unsupervised, a masked slice written into a database on the production primary that is
     feeding the standby it was read from, with no same-cluster warning and no refusal.
attempts_list.fix: Two separate things, and the first is the same defect as the replica attempt above -- fix that and this path closes with it, because both ADR-013 checks are downstream of `Eligibility.SameCluster`. Worth reporting separately because it shows the unsupervised door is open, not only the named-target one: ADR-013's Decision reasons that a named --target is acceptable because the operator chose it, and its second escalation (`target.refused.gate_same_cluster`, `!r.targetNamed && r.headless`) is the whole of what protects the ladder-chosen case; that escalation inherits the gate's false negative verbatim. Second, on the compose half of the surface: internal/discover/containers.go's comment "Every connection-bearing fact comes off these and off the live port bindings, never off a compose file (ADR-008 section 4)" holds -- I could not get a DSN out of a compose file at all, and the production DSN had to come in through rung 2's environment variable instead. That part of the surface is closed by design and the code matches the comment. Suggested hardening independent of the identity fix: ADR-013's discovery-stage check uses `clusterKey` (host and port without the database), which cannot see a standby/primary pair either; when the source answers `pg_is_in_recovery() = true`, a headless run with no --target should refuse outright and name --target, because the ladder has no cheap way to tell a standby's primary from an unrelated server.
